issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בְּרֹאשׁ גֹּלִים' means 'at the head of the exiles' (i.e., they will be first among those exiled), but the Chinese renders it as '在高處露頭' ('appear at a high place'), which changes the meaning. The phrase refers to being led into exile, not being elevated.

The Hebrew 'וְסָר מִרְזַח סְרוּחִים' means 'the revelry of the loungers will pass away' (i.e., the feasting of the self-indulgent will cease), but the Chinese '從邪僻的筵席退去' ('withdraw from the perverse feast') implies the people themselves withdraw from a feast, whereas the Hebrew states the feast itself will come to an end. This reverses the subject and action.
